title: Browser extension (WebExtensions, Manifest V3)
appliesWhen: Any browser extension built on the WebExtensions APIs (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, other Chromium browsers), whether published to a store or distributed privately.
ask: Which browsers and stores will the extension ship to (Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons, Edge Add-ons, Safari, enterprise only), and which sites and user data will it touch?

sources.title: Chrome extensions: Deal with remote hosted code violations
Extension Workshop: Manifest V3 migration guide (Firefox)

guidance: Manifest V3 is the target: Chrome disabled Manifest V2 extensions in Chrome 138 (July 2025) and the Chrome Web Store removed the remaining MV2 extensions on 31 August 2026.

All executable code (JavaScript and WebAssembly) must ship inside the package. Fetching data (JSON, CSS, images, configuration) is allowed; loading scripts from a server, eval and new Function are not. Check dependencies too: SDKs that inject remote scripts (analytics, auth widgets, payment widgets) are the usual cause of store rejections.

The MV3 extension_pages CSP cannot be weaker than script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; object-src 'self'. 'unsafe-eval' is an install-time error in Chrome. Code that must evaluate strings belongs in a sandboxed page (manifest sandbox key), which has no access to extension APIs.

Prefer activeTab, optional_permissions and optional_host_permissions (requested at the moment of use from a user gesture) over broad install-time host permissions such as <all_urls>. Users can revoke host permissions at any time in Chrome and Firefox, so check permissions.contains before relying on them.

Treat content scripts as running in hostile territory: any message from a content script may have been crafted by the page. Validate message shape, check sender.id and sender.url/origin, keep privileged calls and secrets in the background, and never let a content script choose an arbitrary URL to fetch or arbitrary arguments for an extension API.

Only listen to runtime.onMessageExternal when needed, and restrict callers with externally_connectable matches/ids. Keep web_accessible_resources to the files pages truly need, limited by matches; every exposed file lets sites fingerprint the extension.
Do not build DOM from page or server data with innerHTML or document.write; create nodes and set textContent.

storage.local and storage.sync are readable by content scripts and are not encrypted; storage.session is in memory and not exposed to content scripts by default, so use it for tokens and other sensitive values. storage.sync is small (about 100 KB total, 8 KB per item, 120 writes per minute). Local extension storage is cleared on uninstall; data on your servers is not.

Cross-browser background: Chrome MV3 supports only background.service_worker; Firefox does not support service workers and uses background.scripts (event page). Declaring both keys works in Chrome 121+ and Firefox 121+; Safari uses scripts unless preferred_environment says otherwise.

Service workers and event pages are terminated when idle: keep state in storage, register listeners synchronously at top level, and use chrome.alarms instead of setTimeout/setInterval for anything longer than a few seconds.

Chrome now exposes the browser namespace with promises (Chrome 148+); for older Chrome versions or shared code use webextension-polyfill. Firefox needs browser_specific_settings.gecko.id to publish; Firefox gives web_accessible_resources a random per-install UUID, so do not hard-code moz-extension:// URLs.
Build output, not source, is what browsers and reviewers see: run the checks against the packaged directory (dist/ in the gate commands; change it with profile gate … --command).

gates.title: Manifest V3 with a CSP no weaker than the default
gates.setup: Build the extension so the packaged manifest is at dist/manifest.json, or point the command at the built manifest (for example per browser build folder) with profile gate G-EXT-MANIFEST --command "…".
gates.command: node -e "const f=process.argv[1],m=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(f,'utf8')),e=[];if(m.manifest_version!==3)e.push('manifest_version is '+m.manifest_version+', expected 3');const c=m.content_security_policy;if(c&&typeof c!=='object')e.push('content_security_policy must be an object with extension_pages (MV3)');const p=(c&&c.extension_pages)||'';const s=(p.match(/script-src([^;]*)/)||['',''])[1].trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);for(const t of s)if(!['\'self\'','\'wasm-unsafe-eval\''].includes(t))e.push('extension_pages script-src allows '+t);if(/unsafe-eval|unsafe-inline/.test(p.replace('wasm-unsafe-eval','')))e.push('extension_pages CSP relaxes eval or inline script');if(e.length){console.error(f+': '+e.join('; '));process.exit(1)}console.log(f+': MV3, default-or-stricter CSP')" dist/manifest.json
gates.architecture: Record the target browsers and minimum versions, where the built manifest for each browser comes from (hand-written, generated by a framework, merged per browser), and the content_security_policy (default or stricter).
acceptance: The built manifest declares manifest_version 3
content_security_policy.extension_pages, if set, allows only 'self' and 'wasm-unsafe-eval' in script-src and contains no unsafe-eval or unsafe-inline

gates.title: No remotely hosted code in the package
gates.setup: Build first; the command scans dist/ (change the folder with profile gate G-EXT-REMOTE-CODE --command "…"). It catches script tags, import() and importScripts() that load http(s) URLs; review other dynamic loading (script.src assignments, eval, new Function) by hand.
gates.architecture: Record that all executable code is bundled, which third-party SDKs are included and that none loads remote scripts, and what is fetched at runtime (data and configuration only, never logic).
acceptance: The scan of the built package finds no script tags, import() or importScripts() loading http(s) URLs
No eval, new Function or string-based setTimeout in extension code outside a sandboxed page
Remote responses are treated as data and never change which code paths exist

gates.title: Least-privilege permissions and host permissions
gates.architecture: Record a table of every permission and host pattern in the manifest with the feature that needs it, whether it is required or optional (optional_permissions / optional_host_permissions, requested at the moment of use), and why a narrower alternative (activeTab, specific hosts, declarativeNetRequest) is not enough.
acceptance: Every permission and host pattern in the built manifest maps to a feature in the permissions table; nothing is requested for future use
Broad host access (<all_urls>, *://*/*) is absent, or justified in the architecture and requested optionally where the browser allows
Features behind optional or revocable permissions check permissions.contains and degrade gracefully when access is missing, with tests

gates.title: Message passing validates senders and input
gates.architecture: Record every message channel (content script to background, popup/options to background, externally_connectable pages or extensions, native messaging), the message types each accepts, how the sender is checked (sender.id, sender.url or origin, tab), and which privileged actions stay in the background.
acceptance: Every runtime.onMessage / onConnect handler validates the message type and payload and rejects unknown types, with tests
runtime.onMessageExternal is absent, or externally_connectable lists exact matches/ids and the handler checks sender origin or id, with tests
Content scripts cannot make the background fetch an arbitrary URL or call an extension API with caller-chosen arguments
No secrets, tokens or cross-origin data are sent to content scripts

gates.title: Page content handled as untrusted; minimal web-accessible resources
gates.architecture: Record which pages content scripts run on (matches, run_at, world), how they read and change the page, and which web_accessible_resources are exposed and to which matches.
acceptance: No innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML or document.write with page, user or server data in extension or content-script code
Content scripts run only on the sites listed in the architecture; MAIN-world scripts, if any, receive no privileged data
web_accessible_resources lists only the files pages need, restricted by matches

gates.title: User data stored in the right place and transmitted securely
gates.architecture: Record every item of user data the extension keeps, its storage area (storage.session, storage.local, storage.sync, IndexedDB, server), whether content scripts can read it, retention, and how server-side data is deleted when the user asks or uninstalls.
acceptance: Tokens and other sensitive values live in storage.session or on the server, not in storage.local, storage.sync or localStorage
storage.session access level is not widened to content scripts unless the architecture records why
All network requests use HTTPS
Data kept on a server can be deleted on request, with tests

gates.title: Cross-browser manifest and API differences handled
gates.architecture: Record the build per target browser: background (service_worker for Chromium, scripts for Firefox and Safari, or both keys), browser_specific_settings.gecko.id and strict_min_version for Firefox, namespace and promise handling (browser namespace or webextension-polyfill), and APIs unavailable in a target (for example sidePanel vs sidebar_action, debugger and declarativeContent in Firefox).
acceptance: The extension loads without manifest errors in each target browser at its minimum version
Features using browser-specific APIs are feature-detected or built per browser, and the core flow is tested in each target browser
